title: Make a service history accumulate materially
summary: Design a repair-desk surface where status, evidence, and history gather into a lived record instead of a standard dashboard.
originNote: Distilled from a history-derived preference for interfaces where actions leave visible residue and one central record carries the domain.

setup.instructions: Mount the fictional repair packet. Create a self-contained static application with no external dependencies.

turns.content: Read fixtures/repairs.json and build a complete responsive repair-desk interface as index.html. One item's current state should be the central object, while its intake, inspection, parts, work, and pickup events accumulate as a material record a person can revisit. The interface must make the difference between fact, technician note, pending decision, and completed action perceptible without relying on color alone. Include all three repair items and a way to focus each one. Do not use a conventional dashboard of interchangeable statistic cards or reduce the history to a plain data table. Mark the event-history region with data-section="history".

Revise the focused-item transition: changing focus must not make the previous item's material trace feel erased. Preserve the existing visual direction and data, and make continuity visible without adding a dashboard sidebar.

checks.description: The event history is present as an inspectable region.
Switch among all three items and inspect whether prior history retains perceptible residue.
